Market stance

Split tape: iain wants one more flush to trap late shorts before any rip, Remz calls a generational run, and Enrich sees growth selling slowing into a bases-building week — while Friday's quiet index drift left the indexes themselves without a single trader call.

Key watches

Catalysts

  • FOMC Wednesday + PCE Thursday (Enrich) — a massive earnings week on top
  • NVDA at the trendline (Prof) — failed ATH breakout, now sitting on the 30-week MA
  • Monday's open — the first session after the group's Sunday-evening week plans

Market — SPY · QQQ · IWM · TLT

Macro overlay — from their posts, not our data
A busy Sunday-evening tape, and a split one. Sean goes into the week short weakness (MU, ASML, LITE, MRVL, DELL) and conditionally long overextension reversals (GLD, CBRS, LRCX) while tracking relative strength in SHOP, ZETA, IOT, FROG, RBRK and IBM. iain wants one more flush to trap late shorts before a rip, but calls the 9-week bids in CRWD, OKTA, PLTR and NTAP the leadership pivot to watch. Enrich runs the conditional week: market stays weak → oil breakouts (XOM, BP, OXY); growth rebounds → oversold names — with FOMC Wednesday and PCE Thursday as the week's events. Prof's only market-level warning is NVDA at the trendline, plus a CART tease with no level. Remz is the outright bull (generational run) while warning that debt markets have shut off money for companies without revenue independent of AI data centers. Venu adds the discipline note (don't buy dips in deep downtrends) and one quality reclaim (ISRG). DiCarlo posted nothing new in this window. Your process sides with the watchers over the callers: the genuine setups are the confirmed breakouts (FROG, IOT, XOM/BP) and the flag (CRM); everything else is a bounce to watch hold, a short into strength, or a reversal that has not set up yet.

Sean — process, no trades: “Trading is different. Because what do you mean I need to work without getting paid for an undisclosed amount of time…” — quoted to the visible cutoff. His week plan, FROG and IOT calls are rows above.

Sources & Methodology
  • Accounts scanned (7): Sean trades @SRxTrades · iain @ohiain · Enrich Trades @enrichtrades · Remz @Remzztrades · Prof @TheProfInvestor · Venu @Venu_7_ · Peter DiCarlo @pdicarlotrader. All seven profiles were readable this window (top ~5 posts visible per account before the login wall). DiCarlo is the exception on content, not readability: he posted nothing new in this window, so he has no row.
  • Posts window: Sun Oct 25 – Mon Oct 26, 2026 — everything visible after the Oct 25 feed’s window (which ended Oct 25, 11:45 UTC). Logged-out X shows only the ~5 most recent posts per account; posts truncated in the extraction itself (Sean’s week-plan tail and process post, iain’s cash-patience post, Prof’s NVDA and CART posts, Venu’s discipline post, Remz’s debt-markets post, Enrich’s watchlist tail) are quoted only to the visible cutoff.
  • Price data: Yahoo Finance daily data, as of the Fri Oct 23, 2026 close — this run is pre-market Monday, so Friday’s close is the latest completed close and Monday’s session is not in any number here. Trader-stated = a level or call from their post, attributed by name. Chart check = computed by us from that data — it can confirm or push back on a trader’s framing, and it’s labeled every time.
  • Sector lines: each card’s sector/industry ETF comparison (Yahoo Finance, Fri Oct 23, 2026 close) — close, day change, Weinstein stage by the same 30-week MA method, and price vs the 50-week EMA. Mappings: AAPL/NTAP/IBM/IOT/DELL/LITE→XLK, MSFT/FROG/RBRK/PLTR/CRM→IGV, NVDA/MU/ASML/MRVL/CBRS/LRCX→SMH, GOOGL/META/ZETA→XLC, AMZN/TSLA/SHOP/CART→XLY, XOM/BP/OXY→XLE, RKLB→UFO (space — best fit), CRWD/OKTA/ZS→CIBR (cybersecurity — best fit), ISRG→XLV (health care — best fit), GLD→GLD (gold — the name is itself the gold ETF). Best-fit choices are noted here, not hidden.
  • Where none of the seven commented, the section says Unavailable / no trader signal — never “unchanged.” All four indexes are unavailable this window: no trader posted an index-specific level or call (the SPY panel carries iain’s and Remz’s general-market stances, but neither names an index level, so the strip label stays unavailable, as in yesterday’s feed).
  • Qualifier rules (constructive pullback into a key MA/support, tightening base near highs, confirmed breakout; never extended/chased). Flagged qualifiers: FROG and IOT (confirmed breakouts, with the traders’ own charts embedded), XOM and BP (new-high oil breakouts), OXY (cup breakout in progress), CRM (flag breakout valid, $270 target). Constructive holds, not entries: PLTR, ZETA, RBRK, SHOP. Bounce days to watch hold, not chase: CRWD, OKTA, NTAP, ZS. Explicitly not qualifiers: CART (tease after a +9.21% day on 5.07x volume — extended), GLD/CBRS/LRCX (conditional reversal buys with no setup yet — falling knives, not entries), MU/ASML/LITE/DELL (Sean’s shorts, not longs), MRVL (contested — short vs watchlist), RKLB (declining, base watch only), TSLA (pattern watch — $400 not hit), NVDA (at the line — warning, not a setup), ISRG (reclaim attempt, weekly trend not yet turned), AAPL (holds-only at the highs), MSFT/GOOGL/AMZN/META (chart checks only).
  • Coverage note: yesterday’s ideas (CIFR, ARKG, GLXY, VRT) are not carried over — this window’s posts don’t repeat those calls, so they are not rows. DiCarlo’s Oct 24 VRT/GLXY posts fall outside this window and are not repeated here.
  • Badge key: Setup describes structure only (green = constructive, amber = pending confirmation, red = broken/extended). Coverage counts the traders behind a name and is always gray — “Chart only” means no trader mentioned it and implies nothing about the setup. Stage lives in the pill next to each ticker (30-week MA basis) and is kept out of the prose and the setup badges; traders’ own quoted words are exempt. CBRS carries a “No 30-wk history” pill instead of a stage: it IPO’d May 14, 2026 and has only 23 weekly closes, so no 30-week MA or 50-week EMA exists for it yet.
  • Level strength: Strong = 2+ confluent anchors (52w high/low, 3m swing, 50-day EMA, 30-week MA, 50-week EMA, trader-stated) within 0.75%, or a 52w extreme with 3+ weekly touches in the past year. Moderate = 1 anchor or 2–3 touches. Light = anything else. Touches count weeks whose high or low came within 0.75% of the level. Duplicate prices merge into one row carrying both labels.
  • Trader charts: four embedded this edition — Sean’s IOT monthly chart and FROG monthly chart, Enrich’s TSLA cup-&-handle chart and CRM flag chart — retrieved from the photo links in their posts, visually verified as the correct tickers’ charts, and embedded below our charts in their panels with a link back to each post. Prof’s NVDA and CART posts carry media that could not be reliably matched to this window’s posts in the logged-out HTML, so no Prof chart is embedded rather than risking a wrong one.
  • Chart verification gate: every plotted line’s endpoint was checked against levels.json before the HTML was built — all computable lines passed within 0.5% (most within 0.03%). The 30-week MA is a true trailing mean over full 30-week windows only. CBRS’s 30-week MA and 50-week EMA are not applicable (insufficient history) and are shown as such, not estimated.
